newsitem.title: UK: IPE natural gas futures rise, next winter stronges.
newsitem.headline: IPE natural gas futures rise, next winter stronges.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures closed mostly higher on Wednesday, the fourth day of the contract, although the front month, March, softened marginally.
Trade was thin, with only 175 lots traded compared with 280 on Tuesday and a record 465 on Friday, the opening day.
"It's slightly more disappointing," said a broker, adding that most brokers were still not sure of the fundamentals driving the market.

Players on the spot market had expected prices to recover on Wednesday after a sharp fall on Tuesday. The fall had been put down to the fact that many players were long at the end of the winter as a result of stocking up with greater caution than normal to ensure supplies ahead of the first winter under the Network Code.

But prices fell so far on Tuesday that some players said they were near the point when producers would leave gas in the ground and others said it had now become an attractive buy, so adding a bullish tone to the market.

This was reflected on the IPE, with six of the eight monthly contracts which traded moving up. Only January 1998, which was unchanged, and March, the first month, which fell by 0.10 pence a therm, bucked the trend.

"There were a few cross trades this morning for next winter," said a broker. "They were the first trades done this morning and established the market highs. It may have distorted the picture slightly."
But he noted that the mid-months of June, July and August were also stronger, although there was "not a lot of activity."
